summary: The new announcement window contains no major heavy-ion collision result. The strongest paper is instead a well-validated generative surrogate for FCC-ee detector simulation and reconstruction; useful companion work applies optimal transport to negative-weight mitigation and full-phase-space validation, while a physics-informed spectral solver has plausible but still untested transfer value for heavy-ion inverse problems.
professional_summary: Generative detector surrogates with downstream validation; optimal-transport metrics for negative-weight mitigation and reweighting validation; information bounds for rapidity-window multiplicities; stiff physics-informed PDE solvers.
strongest_paper: 2609.30775: generative surrogate for full CLD detector simulation and reconstruction
strongest_paper_summary: Parnassus combines broad distribution checks, held-out-flavor tests, downstream flavor-tagging validation, public artifacts, and an end-to-end speed benchmark.

papers.title: Parnassus for the CLD Detector: A Generative Machine-Learning Surrogate for Detector Simulation and Reconstruction at the FCC-ee
papers.summary: A conditional flow-matching model emulates the combined Geant4-plus-PandoraPFA CLD response. It reproduces particle, jet, event, impact-parameter, and flavor-dependent distributions; a frozen full-simulation flavor tagger transfers with only a 0.012 absolute accuracy loss, while generation costs about 1.3 ms per event on an A100 versus about 6 s for full simulation and reconstruction on one CPU core.
papers.abstract: The model is trained on 2.125 million Z to qq and Z to bb events, tested on 500,000 events including held-out strange and charm flavors, and benchmarked against Delphes. Public code and data accompany the 32-page study.

papers.title: Optimizing Cell-Based Negative Weight Mitigation with Optimal Transport
papers.summary: Cell resampling uses an infrared- and collinear-safe optimal-transport distance to redistribute negative event weights locally. On roughly 100,000 NLO Z+jets events, reweighting 75% of cells reduces the inverse Kish effective sample fraction from 16 to 6 and introduces less bias than the earlier Euclidean metric.
papers.abstract: The proof-of-concept compares transport-based and Euclidean event metrics, evaluates full-phase-space and observable-level bias, and finds the hadron-level transport metric most stable. Code and datasets are public.

papers.title: A Phase-Space Inclusive Figure of Merit Based in Optimal Transport for Validating Monte Carlo Reweightings
papers.summary: The paper adapts the Cross-Section-Mover's Distance into an unbinned, projection-independent diagnostic for full-phase-space reweighting bias. Its immediate value is as a companion validation tool for negative-weight mitigation, with a credible extension to detector surrogates and generative event models.
papers.abstract: The eight-page CHEP proceedings paper defines an event-level energy-mover distance and a theory-level transport distance, then demonstrates them on several negative-weight reweighting schemes.

papers.title: An information bound for multiplicities in rapidity windows of the dipole cascade behind the entanglement entropy picture
papers.summary: For a one-dimensional Mueller dipole cascade, the authors derive a ceiling of one-half log(4/3) on a Gaussian proxy for conditional mutual information between outer rapidity windows at fixed middle multiplicity. Detector losses and independent window migration preserve the compound-counting law, but transverse-dimensional cascade simulations violate the single-source assumption and H1 multiplicity moments disfavor its simplest one-dipole realization.
papers.abstract: The work provides exact compound-counting relations, factorial-cumulant consistency tests, extensive reproducibility files, and an explicit failure test once transverse cascade dynamics are restored.

papers.title: NEXT: Physics-Informed Neuro-Spectral Exponential Time Differencing Architectures
papers.summary: NEXT integrates the stiff linear part of a spectral PDE discretization exactly with exponential time differencing and learns only the nonlinear remainder. It is stable where the parent NeuSA method diverges and supports sparse-data inverse problems, but all evidence is from canonical PDE benchmarks rather than realistic multi-dimensional physics workloads.
papers.abstract: Benchmarks cover heat, wave, Burgers, and KdV equations plus coefficient and boundary-flux inference. Code is public, and fourth-order integration substantially improves accuracy at higher training cost.

cautions.title: Point-cloud generative models for fast calorimeter simulation across particles and geometries
cautions.summary: The headline is attractive: one point-cloud program covers electromagnetic, hadronic, multi-particle, and cross-geometry calorimeter simulation, with a reported 120-fold CPU speedup for one component. However, this is a six-page proceedings synthesis of several projects, so it does not provide enough unified validation to support the broad claim as a single new result.
cautions.abstract: The contribution summarizes CaloClouds3, CaloHadronic, AllShowers, and cross-geometry transfer learning rather than presenting a standalone end-to-end validation study.
